To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the skin permeation and transdermal flux of ibuprofen can be enhanced by POE alkyl ethers and the mechanism of the enhancing effect of POE alkyl ethesr on the skin permeability of ibuprofen may be attributed to the formation of hydrogen bonds between the POE alkyl and ibuprofen.
the POE alkyl ethers containing the EO chain lengths of 2-10, HLB values of 7-10 and C16-C18 alkyl chain length were effective promoters of skin permeation of 5% ibuuprofen.

polyoxyethylene (5) cetyl/oleyl ethers (HLB = 7.9) and polyoxyethylene (2) lauryl ether (HLB =9.0) were found to be the most effective enhancers in promoting skin permeation of the non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug, ibuprofen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of transdermal formulations for ibuprofen using polyoxyethylene (EO) alkyl ethers as enhancers.
the development of new formulations containing polyethoxylate surfactants as transdermal drug delivery systems.
the influence of polyethyoxylated surfactants on transdermal permeation of ibuuprofen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transdermal delivery of ibuprofen can be improved by the use of a series of POE alkyl ethers.
POE(2)cetyl/olelyl ether is the most suitable formulation vehicle for the transdermal delivery of ibuprofen.
the skin permeation rate of ibuprofen is dependent on the EO chain length, the HLB value and the alkyl chain length.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
POE(2)-oleyl ether, POE(5)-cetyl/oleyl and POE(2)cetyl ethers were the best enhancers for ibuprofen.
POE alkyl ethers with a suitable alkyl chain length, an EO chain length of less than five, and an HLB value between 7 and 9 were effective promoters of transdermal permeation of ibiprofen.
a new transdermal formulation of ibuprofen using POE alkyl ethers was developed and the physicochemical interaction between the ibupropfen and POE alkyl ethers was investigated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of polyoxyethylene ethers can improve skin permeability and the use of these surfactants in a transdermal delivery system is a promising approach for improving skin permeability of drugs.
POE alkyl ethers can be used as a transdermal enhancer for ibuprofen.
the polyoxyethylene alkylethers with a HLB range of 7-10 can be used as effective promoters for the skin permeation enhancement of ibuprofen.
